prompt:
Locked-off camera, no zoom, no pan. On the right, the tall black server cabinet on small castors rolls straight ahead, away from the camera, down the open floor beside the rope lane toward the POWER counters at the back of the hall. It is very heavy: it starts slowly, gathers a steady walking pace, and moves as one rigid box, its castors turning and its bundle of grey cables sliding and dragging across the floor behind it. The green and blue lights on its front blink in irregular patterns as it goes. On the left, the three in the queue turn their heads to follow it, open-mouthed: the woman in the mustard coat clutching the white kettle, the pensioner in the lilac coat with silver curls holding the small fan, the red-haired lad in the grey hoodie behind them. At about four seconds the pensioner leans slightly toward it and says quietly, with prim indignation, "There's a queue, love." Her lips move in time with exactly those words; the other two stay silent. The machine carries on rolling toward the counters without stopping. The people at the counters in the background stay where they are. Every POWER sign keeps its exact letters. Same light throughout.
Natural documentary realism, overcast daylight.
Thanks.
